jobs.title: Senior Director, Corporate Strategy & Development
jobs.description:
Are you ready to embark on a career that truly affects people around the world? Trulioo invites you to be a catalyst for change in the dynamic realm of digital identity verification. As the global front-runner in our industry, we are redefining how businesses grow, innovate and comply online.

Picture yourself at the forefront of innovation, contributing to our award-winning platform that enables organizations worldwide to quickly onboard customers, optimize costs and combat fraud. Fueled by Silicon Valley support, Trulioo stands as the trusted platform that can verify more than 5 billion people and 700 million business entities spanning 195 countries.

But Trulioo is more than a tech company. We are a united force of dedicated experts committed to establishing trust online - and we’re proud to be recognized as a BC Top Employer for the second consecutive year
, reflecting our commitment to an inclusive, collaborative, and people-first workplace.

Headquartered in Vancouver and with strategic hubs in San Diego and Dublin, we foster a culture of collaboration and open communication. Our offices support a hybrid model and staff typically work three days per week at a hub location. Join us where excitement meets innovation and contribute to a world where trust and technology unite.

What We Offer

Comprehensive Benefits: We provide a robust benefits package for full-time, permanent employees, including health, dental, and vision coverage, retirement plans with company match, paid time off, parental leave, and an annual education & training stipend (equivalent to $1,000 in local currency). Specific benefits may vary by location and will be discussed further during the interview process.
Flexible Hybrid Working Environment: Our offices are designed to support both collaboration and flexibility. Enjoy weekly lunches, quality coffee, and regular social events. Many locations also feature parent rooms, on-site gyms, comfortable lounges, and adaptable workstations to support your comfort and productivity.
Wellness: We care about your well-being. Team members have access to wellness workshops and events, as well as a complimentary Headspace subscription to help you stay focused, grounded, and energized.
Employee Resource Groups: Belonging is an important part of doing your best work. Our ERGs provide an inclusive space, support and community for employees of diverse backgrounds and allies. We host informative, fun sessions and celebrations that are often open to the entire organization.

Position Summary

Trulioo is seeking a Senior Director of Corporate Strategy & Development to help shape the company’s strategic direction and translate it into coordinated action across the business. Working closely with the Chief Risk & Strategy Officer, this leader will own the continued evolution of Trulioo’s strategic blueprint, strengthen alignment between corporate strategy and functional priorities, and guide execution of the company’s most important strategic initiatives.

This role will build the intelligence, governance, and execution capabilities that allow Trulioo to anticipate market change and make informed choices about where and how to compete. The Senior Director will bring together customer, competitive, regulatory, economic, industry, and product insights to test strategic assumptions, identify emerging opportunities and risks, and inform decisions across organic investment, partnerships, and acquisitions.

This is a highly visible enterprise leadership role at the intersection of strategy, product, transformation, capital allocation, and corporate development. The ideal candidate combines forward-looking strategic judgment with the ability to operationalize ideas—building roadmaps, mobilizing accountable leaders, guiding complex programs, and creating the governance needed to turn strategy into measurable results.

This role is expected to leverage AI and emerging technologies to improve productivity, enhance decision-making, and continuously optimize how work is performed.

This will be a full-time, permanent position, working remotely.

What You'll Be Doing

Corporate Strategy and Strategic Blueprint Support

Continuously test the strategy against market forces, competitive dynamics, regulatory developments, customer needs, technology shifts, and emerging opportunity areas.
Partner with the Chief Risk & Strategy Officer to prepare strategic recommendations and decision materials for executives, the Board, external advisors, and other key stakeholders.
Design scenario analyses that evaluate strategic assumptions, alternative market outcomes, competitive responses, investment choices, and potential disruptions.
Identify material risks to the strategy and partner with the Enterprise Risk Office to assess exposure, define responses, and integrate strategic risks into enterprise governance.
Develop clear points of view on competitive positioning, market adjacencies, thematic investments, and the capabilities Trulioo will need to win over the long term.
Co-lead recurring strategy reviews and recommend when elements of the strategic blueprint should be accelerated, refined, reprioritized, or recast.

Strategy Alignment and Execution

Translate the strategic blueprint into enterprise priorities, functional goals, measurable outcomes, and clear execution roadmaps.
Partner with executive and functional leaders to align their strategies, investments, roadmaps, OKRs, KPIs, and/or incentives with the company’s strategic direction.
Define the scope, activities, sequencing, investment requirements, accountabilities, dependencies, and measures of success for major strategic programs.
Establish and chair governance forums that track progress against strategic priorities and create clear paths for decision-making and escalation.
Partner with the Transformation Office and accountable workstream leaders to mobilize initiatives, resolve cross-functional blockers, measure progress and performance, and redirect execution when outcomes move off course.
Create recurring feedback loops, including shared metrics reviews and strategy check-ins, to identify misalignment early and improve execution.
Communicate the strategy across the organization in ways that build understanding of Trulioo’s direction, strategic choices, and highest-priority activities.

MAPS and Capital Allocation Governance

Lead MAPS—Trulioo’s quarterly Market Aligned Product Strategy program—to connect corporate strategy and market intelligence with product strategy, investment decisions, and roadmaps.
Bring together Product, Engineering, Strategy, Risk and Reg, Sales, Marketing, and GTM leaders to evaluate emerging customer needs and market opportunities.
Guide structured decisions on whether Trulioo should build, buy, partner, watch, or pass in response to identified opportunities.
Oversee the development of MAPS insight packages covering regulatory change, voice of the customer, competitive moves, market potential, cost of missed opportunity, industry trends, and product performance.
In coordination with the Office of the CFO, develop and operate a disciplined capital allocation governance program that connects strategic priorities with investment decisions.
Build decision frameworks that clarify opportunity, strategic fit, expected value, investment requirements, trade-offs, risks, and measures of success.
Produce a forward-looking point of view on capital allocation priorities informed by Trulioo’s competitive position, portfolio performance, and emerging growth opportunities.

Corporate Development and M&A

Support the development of Trulioo’s Build, Buy, and Partner strategy by identifying capability gaps and evaluating inorganic paths to accelerate the strategic blueprint.
Support market mapping, opportunity screening, target identification, strategic fit assessments, and ongoing target monitoring.
Coordinate cross-functional due diligence, including workstream planning, information synthesis, issue escalation, decision support, and executive reporting.
Contribute to due diligence activities and deal-structure considerations in partnership with Finance, Legal, Product, Technology, Risk, and external advisors.
Develop scalable models, AI agents, and analytical tools that strengthen opportunity screening, target intelligence, diligence, and transaction decision-making.
Capture relevant integration considerations during diligence and translate findings into clear implications for value creation, execution complexity, and transaction risk.

Market Insights and Strategic Intelligence

Design and operate Trulioo’s enterprise market insights program as a continuously running intelligence engine for strategy, product development, investment, and commercialization.
Produce forward-looking insights, including market landscapes, competitive positioning, opportunity sizing, thematic investment perspectives, regulatory outlooks, and voice-of-the-customer analysis.
Build repeatable methods for gathering, validating, synthesizing, and distributing intelligence across the organization.
Translate complex signals into clear strategic implications, executive-level reporting, and actionable recommendations.
Deliver relevant insights to executives, Product, Engineering, Risk and Regulatory, Marketing, Sales, and GTM teams through recurring briefings, dashboards, decision forums, and targeted analyses.
Develop measures that demonstrate how market intelligence improves strategic decisions, product prioritization, capital allocation, and commercial outcomes.

What You'll Bring

15+ years of experience across corporate strategy, corporate development, strategic finance, management consulting, market intelligence, transformation, or related leadership roles.
Significant experience in one or more relevant sectors, including payments, financial services, banking, marketplaces, SaaS, fintech, identity, fraud, or RegTech.
A degree in economics, business, finance, strategy, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
A builder mindset and strong experience working and deploying AI tools and models to improve functional processes, drive automation, rethink problem solving, and transform traditional ways of working.
Demonstrated experience developing corporate or product strategies and translating them into enterprise priorities, functional roadmaps, investment decisions, and measurable outcomes.
Experience operating in complex, global, and highly cross-functional organizations.
Experience leading large-scale strategic or transformation programs involving multiple executives, functions, and dependencies.
Meaningful experience supporting acquisitions, including opportunity assessment, target screening, due diligence, transaction analysis, and integration planning.
Advanced analytical and scenario-planning capabilities, with the ability to work through ambiguity and make clear recommendations from incomplete or conflicting information.
Exceptional executive communication skills and experience preparing materials for executive leadership, Boards, and external advisors.
The judgment and executive presence to influence senior leaders, challenge assumptions, facilitate difficult trade-offs, and drive decisions.

Nice To Have

Exposure to identity verification, fraud prevention, credit insights, financial crime, or regulatory technology.
Experience supporting IPO readiness, public-company strategy, or Board-level capital allocation processes.
Direct experience leading post-acquisition integration or value-creation programs.
An advanced degree in economics, business, finance, or a related discipline.

University degree and a professional accounting designation (CPA/CA or equivalent).

Experience overseeing external service providers and working with auditors to maintain effective internal controls and audit readiness.
Strong financial systems skills, including advanced Excel. Experience with Mercatus, Workiva or Anaplan is an asset.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, organizational and communication skills, with the judgment to anticipate risks and advise senior management.
Proactive and accountable, with the ability to manage competing priorities, adapt quickly and meet deadlines in a complex, fast-paced environment.

jobs.title: President
jobs.description:
President: lead a specialty piling contractor to $50M

VersaPile Inc. | Alberta or Manitoba | Reports to the Founder and Executive Chair

If you have run piling operations, you already know what most construction executives never learn: schedules move, ground conditions surprise you, receivables slip, and critical equipment fails far from major centres. If that sounds like a normal week, and you are good at it, keep reading. If it sounds exhausting, this is not your job.

The mission

Our founder is moving to Executive Chair, and we are hiring a President to take over day-to-day leadership of the company.
Run VersaPile day to day and help turn a fast-growing, dynamic business into a mature and predictable one.
Build the systems and leaders that make clients treat VersaPile as an extension of their own team.
Lead a 100% Indigenous-owned company that combines Indigenous ways of thinking with strong Western business practice.
Help drive the company toward becoming Canada's leader in high-capacity helical piles for energy and utilities.

Why this seat is rare

You get the whole company.
The leadership team reports to you.
The platform is built.
We have operations in Alberta and Manitoba, about 35 full-time staff, and what is likely the country's most capable high-capacity helical pile fleet.
Blue-chip clients.
They include Enbridge, Suncor, CNRL, Worley, Valard, Forbes Bros., Aecon, Hydro One and Manitoba Hydro.
High-bar project sites.
Our clients demand excellence in safety, quality and execution, and so do we.
You win when we win.
The compensation package will be designed for the successful candidate to win alongside the company.

What you will deliver

In your first 12 months

The leadership team reports to you in practice, not just on the org chart.
The annual plan is met on safety, revenue, margin and cash.
The org chart is restructured into one that supports who we are today and where we are going, and every leadership seat is held by someone you would rehire.
Clients and partners see continuity through the leadership transition and notice the improvements.

Within three years

75% of revenue comes from repeat clients.
More than 66% of the business is in energy and utilities.
At least 25% of the workforce is Indigenous, and at least 25% of vendor spend goes to Indigenous suppliers.
VersaPile is in a strong financial position, with cash reserves and shareholder distributions.

You are our person if

You have 10 or more years in piling and deep foundations, or in closely related trades such as transmission and distribution construction, pipeline, specialty drilling, heavy civil or industrial earthworks.
You have carried full profit-and-loss responsibility for a project-based business of $30M or more.
You have personally negotiated contracts, change orders, payment terms and holdback releases with clients who still want to work with you.
You manage cash as closely as margin.
You have led through a crisis, and you know what to do in the first hour and the first week.
You build leaders, hold them accountable, and turn ideas into plans.
You will report effectively to the founder and Executive Chair, and to our Advisory Board.

Experience working with Indigenous communities and businesses is an asset. Indigenous candidates are encouraged to apply.

This is not for you if

You need a stable schedule and a plan that survives the week.
Your experience is in general contracting, where you control the schedule.
You hand hard client conversations to a lawyer or a project manager.
You manage from the office instead of leading across regions and sites.
You see Indigenous ownership as a line in a proposal rather than something that shapes hiring, purchasing and daily decisions.

Compensation and location

A comprehensive executive compensation package may include a combination of base salary, performance incentives, phantom equity, benefits, RRSP match and a vehicle.
You will live in Alberta or Manitoba and travel regularly between the two regions.

How to apply

Send your resume and a short note, one page at most, answering these three questions:
What is the largest profit and loss you have personally owned, and what happened to revenue and margin while you owned it?
Describe the hardest commercial negotiation you have led with a client. What was at stake, and how did it end?
What is the most challenging or complex change initiative you have led? What did the initiative achieve?

We read every note. Applications without one will not be considered.

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
Toronto or Waterloo, hybrid | Full-time | Reports to the CEO

Compensation: $160,000 to $190,000 CAD base salary

Build the finance function at a fast-growing senior care technology company shipping hardware to 24 countries.

The Company

We went from a lab in Waterloo to 24 countries in five years. Our sensors detect falls and track sleep, health and wellness, with no cameras, wearables or pendants. Families get peace of mind. Older adults keep their independence. Our CTO, Dr. Yihong Qi, holds 680 patents, and the next few hundred get built here.

Why now

We are scaling. One of the largest deals in our history is in delivery, and our consumer product launches in January. Both run on numbers leadership can trust: a close that lands on time, a forecast that ties sales to inventory and cash, and books that hold up to audit. This is the moment to bring in the leader who owns it.

The role

This is the senior finance role at Pontosense. You own the close, the forecast and controls across our entities in Canada and China. You work directly with the CEO and the leadership team, and you are in the room with investors. This is a builder role first and an operator role second. You set up how finance runs here, then you run it.

What You'll Own

A monthly close that is reliable and consolidated across Canada and China, landing by business day 10
A forecast the company actually runs on, with sales, inventory and cash tied together
Product costing that is right: landed cost, COGS and inventory planning for hardware built overseas
Investor reporting: the financial model and board and investor updates
Annual financials prepared and audited on time, and the relationships with our auditors and tax advisors
Controls that hold up across two countries: approvals, spend and intercompany
A seat at the leadership table

What Year One Looks Like

The books close on time every month, consolidated. The forecast is trusted, and inventory is planned, not guessed. Audited financials are current, and the numbers hold up to any scrutiny.

How We Work

Build it right, then make it better. People's safety rides on what we ship, so we test hard and never settle for good enough.
Say it as it is. Kind and direct, at every level, including the CEO.
Real impact. There is more room to make a difference here than at a company ten times our size.
Do what you said. Trust is built on follow-through, and we return it with real ownership.
Hard, and worth it. What we build keeps someone's parent safe at home. Rest well, it's part of the job.

This is for you if

You'd rather own a problem than be assigned a task
You want the mission to matter and the pace to be real
You're happy to be the person who just fixes it

This isn't for you if

You want a playbook handed to you
You need a big team before you can move

You'll thrive here if

You are a CPA who started in audit, then grew with a product or technology company, with promotions along the way
You have owned the close and built the model yourself, not just reviewed them
You have run FP&A, not only the close: budgets, forecasts and the model leadership makes decisions on
You have worked with inventory, COGS and supply chain costing. Multi-entity or international consolidation is a strong plus
You have worked with investors, a board or lenders, or are ready to step into that
You explain the numbers plainly to people outside finance, and decide with incomplete information
You are as happy reconciling an account yourself as setting the strategy

You don't need to check every box. If this sounds like you, we'd like to hear from you.

Where this goes

As we scale, this role grows into leading a finance team of your own.

What You Get

A sensor for your parents, on us
Direct access to the leadership team. No layers.
Fair pay, with the opportunity for equity
Impact decides your pay and your path, not tenure
Hybrid in Toronto or Waterloo, remote if that's where you do your best work
Health, dental and vision benefits

The details

Pay: $160,000 to $190,000 CAD base salary
This is a new role, created to grow the team, not a backfill
How we hire: typically an initial interview, a short case, and a final interview in person with our CEO and members of the team. We may adjust this depending on the role
We leverage AI tools in our hiring process, but prioritize human input and manual review

Our Commitment

At Pontosense, we are committed to creating a workplace that is inclusive and accessible to all. We value diversity and believe that everyone deserves an equal opportunity to succeed.

If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation during the hiring process, please let us know. We will work with you to make the necessary accommodations to ensure a fair and positive experience for all applicants.

We strive to provide accessible communication and technology for our employees and customers and always look for ways to improve. If you have any feedback or suggestions on how we can improve accessibility in our workplace, please don't hesitate to contact us.

We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and welcome candidates from all backgrounds to apply for open positions at our company.

jobs.title: Director of Finance - Mining
jobs.description:
The Opportunity:

ML6 is partnering with a publicly traded mining organization to identify a Director of Finance to join its growing leadership team.

This individual will play a critical role in overseeing the company's financial reporting, technical accounting, regulatory compliance and internal control environment across its Canadian and international operations.

Reporting directly to the Chief Financial Officer, the Director of Finance will lead the financial reporting function, oversee external audits and ensure the integrity of consolidated financial statements and regulatory disclosures. The position will also provide financial leadership across international subsidiaries, supporting the complexities of operating within a global mining and mineral processing business.

This is an excellent opportunity for a technically strong accounting leader who combines public company reporting experience with a hands-on approach to financial management. jobs.title: Chief Marketing and Strategy Officer
jobs.description:
THE OPPORTUNITY

We have a dynamic opportunity for a Chief Marketing and Strategy Officer (CMSO) to join the Executive Leadership Team at Alberta Municipalities in Edmonton, Alberta. Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, the CMSO is the enterprise integrator for strategy, corporate planning and governance, strategic project management, growth and innovation, and marketing and communications. This is a great role for a leader that thrives in a fast paced and complex senior leadership role, managing multiple competing priorities, in an agile decision-making hub for member priorities. The corporate governance oversight and accountabilities associated with the role are significant and deep experience with Board governance is necessary for success.

The CMSO leads five direct reports: four Senior Directors, responsible for Corporate Planning and Governance, Project Management, Growth and Innovation, and Marketing and Communications, and a Project Coordinator/Executive Assistant. Working in a multifaceted environment, the CMSO makes sense of complex and emerging issues, frames them for decisions by the Chief Executive Officer, the Executive Leadership Team, Boards and Committees, and leads the plans, programs and projects that turn strategy into measurable results for members.

THE IDEAL CANDIDATE

The ideal candidate is a senior strategic leader who thrives in complexity, is a strong and effective communicator and has a deep background in corporate governance. The CMSO will turn ambiguous and competing information into clear strategy and plain language so that Boards, elected officials and executives can act on and set priorities across the organization aligning resources where they create the most value. They bring strong business and corporate service acumen along with a delivery focused mindset that can balance delegating vs perfection, and the judgement and diplomacy to advise on sensitive matters. They will also have the experience and background to effectively work with internal and external partners and stakeholders as well as elected officials and various levels of government.

As a true partner and a leader of people, the successful candidate brings strong emotional intelligence, integrity, a corporate services mindset, earns trust, and builds alignment through influence. They adjudicate objectively between competing views, support productive debate, contribute to dialogue constructively, lean into difficult conversations and step in directly when the team is stretched. They coach senior leaders, draw on the experience of the team, model the organization’s values, and strengthen a collaborative, accountable and high-performing culture, staying calm and fact based in a fast-moving, political environment. They also need to be passionate about the work of municipalities and the people they lead.

THE ORGANIZATION

Founded in 1905, Alberta Municipalities (ABmunis) is the province’s largest municipal association. It represents 264 of Alberta’s 334 municipalities, from small summer villages to major cities and specialized municipalities, which together are home to more than 85% of Albertans. It advocates on shared municipal issues and helps members build resilient communities. It also pools its members’ purchasing power to secure better pricing on employee benefits, insurance, energy and other services, with the proceeds helping fund its advocacy work. Its business services and its advocacy reinforce each other, and it works through partnerships to build common solutions with its members.

Governance

Alberta Municipalities is led by a Board of Directors elected by member municipalities during each annual convention. The Board is comprised of representatives from Alberta’s cities, towns, villages, summer villages, and specialized municipalities.

Additional information about Alberta Municipalities and key resources relevant to this opportunity are available below:
Alberta Municipalities website
2026 Advocacy Priorities
ABmunis Media Releases
ABmunis 2025 year in review

RESPONSIBILITIES

Strategic Leadership and Issues Management

Lead how the organization identifies, assesses and responds to complex and emerging issues, risks and opportunities, drawing on governance, member, advocacy, business, financial, operational, technology and reputational perspectives.
Distill ambiguous issues into clear problem statements, strategic choices and recommendations, and advise the Chief Executive Officer, the Executive Leadership Team and the Boards on significant and sensitive matters.
Develop frameworks, strategies and roadmaps with clear priorities, accountabilities and measures of success, and lead cross functional work on issues that span departments, entities or governance bodies.
Help develop advocacy strategies that advance member priorities with different levels of government and stakeholder groups, building alignment among people with different mandates and perspectives.

Corporate Planning and Governance

Provide executive leadership for governance across multiple (5) Boards, (9) committees and legal entities, respecting their distinct mandates and regulatory requirements, including agenda planning, decision support, appointments and the implementation of Board direction, and ensure Board and committee meetings are well run, with timely, high-quality materials.
Lead strategic planning and evaluation with the Chief Executive Officer, the Executive Leadership Team and the Boards, turning Board direction into organizational priorities, initiatives and performance measures.
Direct environmental scanning of political, economic, social, regulatory, member, market and technology trends, and advance governance effectiveness and Board development.
Oversee the corporate policy framework so policies are developed, reviewed, approved, communicated and applied consistently, in line with legislation and strategy, and oversee Board election processes, including Returning Officer responsibilities.

Strategy Execution and Program/Project Management

Lead the Project Management Office, setting the approach to prioritization, intake, governance, resourcing, risk and reporting, and the level of involvement based on an initiative’s complexity, risk and impact.
Oversee a portfolio of strategic and operational initiatives, including digital transformation (enterprise systems, data, CRM, automation), organizational and process transformation, governance initiatives, business growth, member programs, advocacy and public policy campaigns, and complex regulatory and compliance implementations.
Ensure major initiatives have clear objectives, scope, accountabilities, resources, timelines, risks and success measures before implementation, resolve competing priorities and capacity constraints with sponsors, and keep senior leaders and Boards informed of progress, risks and results.

Growth and Innovation

Lead the department that advances growth, innovation and sustainable revenue, strengthening existing business lines and developing new profitable ones through new markets, partnerships, customer segments, products, services and pricing.
Ensure opportunities are supported by market, financial, operational, governance, legal, tax and risk analysis, and turned into business cases and plans for the Executive Leadership Team and Boards that fit strategy, capacity and mandate.
Lead the adoption of artificial intelligence across the organization with sound governance, privacy, security, risk and change management and training, and watch for emerging technologies and business models that create member value.

Marketing and Communications

Provide strategic direction for marketing, brand, communications and major events, aligned with strategy, advocacy priorities, business objectives and member needs, with resources focused on the greatest value and a clear view of the return on major marketing spend.
Oversee major campaigns and events, including advertising, the annual Convention, advocacy and election campaigns, member engagement and brand initiatives, and guide internal communications so employees receive clear, timely and consistent information.
Translate complex organizational, policy and business issues into clear messages for members, elected officials, partners and other audiences.
Direct sensitive communications issues and media relations, shaping positioning and messaging with other executives to protect the organization’s reputation in a dynamic political environment.
Oversee marketing and brand strategy to strengthen awareness of Alberta Municipalities and its services and support the growth and positioning of its business lines.

Executive and People Leadership

Contribute to the leadership, direction and performance of the organization as a member of the Executive Leadership Team, and act on behalf of the Chief Executive Officer when assigned.
Coach the Senior Directors, set clear expectations and performance measures, and hold leaders accountable for results.
Build a collaborative, accountable and high performing culture that values member focus, strategic thinking, innovation and continuous improvement, and support strong relationships across departments, entities, Boards and committees.

QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum of 15 years of progressively senior experience in strategic planning, corporate governance, organizational strategy, program or project management, public administration or a similarly complex environment.
Significant experience leading enterprise strategic and corporate planning and delivering major cross functional programs and projects involving multiple departments, stakeholders and competing priorities.
Demonstrated experience working within complex governance and decision-making structures involving multiple Boards, committees, organizations or stakeholder groups.
Strong financial and business acumen, including assessing business cases, budgets, contracts, revenue opportunities, costs and risks.
Knowledge of governance practices, change management and innovation, with a strong understanding of economic, social, environmental, technological and political trends and their impact on members.
A degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Political Science, Strategic Management, Organizational Leadership or a related field.

Assets include
:
Master’s degree.
Project Management Professional (PMP), Prosci change management certification or related professional designation.
Experience in a government, municipal, association, regulatory, political or other multi stakeholder environment.
Executive oversight of corporate planning and governance, growth and innovation, a project management office, or marketing, communications, engagement, brand strategy and major events.

KEY COMPETENCIES

Sets long-term strategy with other leaders, owns strategic goals and plans, presents strong business cases for initiatives and resource allocation, and anticipates obstacles and business disruptions.
Analyzes ambiguous information, applies frameworks where there is little precedent, seeks diverse views and makes sound decisions with organization wide consequences.
Delivers clear strategic messages at the enterprise level, explains complex issues in plain language to senior executives and gains buy in and consensus from people with widely different views.
Builds alliances inside and outside the organization and uses a deep understanding of their network to connect people in ways that create value.
Sets performance goals and metrics, approves budgets and investments in line with financial goals, holds leaders accountable and pushes the organization to higher standards.
Anticipates member needs and builds service into goals, programs, products and processes, and fosters a service orientation across the management team.
Breaks down silos and builds an inclusive, consultative culture of collaboration across departments, entities and partners, taking ownership of team and organizational outcomes.

ROLE BOUNDARY -
This is a second-line compliance leadership role. Day-to-day supervision of Approved Persons, new-account approvals, trade reviews and suitability decisions remain with the Branch Manager role. Compliance program leadership

Lead the day-to-day operation of the firm’s compliance program and manage execution of the annual compliance plan.
Maintain the compliance risk assessment, compliance calendar and risk-based testing framework.
Establish monitoring methodologies, documentation standards, quality controls and escalation protocols.
Prioritize resources and continually enhance the effectiveness, efficiency and scalability of the compliance function.

Monitoring and testing oversight

Design and oversee risk-based monitoring and testing of compliance and supervisory controls.

Review testing results, trends, recurring deficiencies and emerging risks.
Challenge supervisory effectiveness and oversee remediation plans and validation testing.
Escalate material findings, high-risk matters and unresolved issues to the CCO.

Branch review program management

Approve the annual review schedule, risk-based scope and testing approach.
Review and approve branch review reports and assess the significance of findings.
Monitor management responses, remediation commitments and overdue actions.
Ensure branch review coverage remains appropriate as the business evolves.

Registration, licensing and continuing education oversight

Oversee registration, licensing, NRD administration, onboarding and termination activities.
Review complex registration matters, restrictions and outside activity disclosures.
Oversee the continuing education, proficiency, annual training and attestation programs.
Ensure registration and proficiency records remain complete, accurate and regulator-ready.

Complaints, investigations and regulatory reporting

Oversee complaint handling, investigations, resolution recommendations and regulatory event assessments.
Review required regulatory notifications, filings and reporting submissions.
Ensure matters are handled consistently, fairly and within applicable requirements.
Escalate material complaints, reportable events and significant conduct concerns to the CCO.

Regulatory examinations and reviews

Lead operational preparation for CIRO examinations, regulatory reviews, audits and information requests.
Coordinate document production, response drafting, examination logistics and internal stakeholders.
Oversee deficiency responses, remediation plans and progress reporting.
Support the CCO in regulator interactions and on material examination matters.

Regulatory change, policies and training

Monitor regulatory developments and conduct impact assessments and gap analyses.
Coordinate implementation of regulatory changes across policies, procedures, controls and business practices.
Maintain compliance policies, guidance and communications and oversee the annual policy review cycle.
Develop and deliver practical training and awareness initiatives.

Governance and reporting

Prepare clear, decision-useful compliance reporting for senior management and governance forums.
Develop dashboards, metrics and key risk indicators and maintain issue and remediation tracking.
Assist the CCO with annual compliance reporting and other governance materials.
Ensure significant matters are escalated on a timely basis.

Team leadership and development

Manage and develop Compliance Officer(s) and future compliance resources.
Establish clear goals, priorities, performance expectations and quality standards.
Review work product and provide coaching, feedback and mentorship.
Build team capability, accountability and succession depth.

Strategic advisory and broader regulatory support

Advise business leaders on regulatory requirements, compliance risks and practical controls for new initiatives and operational changes.
Provide oversight and guidance across AML, privacy, FATCA/CRS, CASL, marketing and communications, conflicts of interest, personal trading, outside activities, registered plans and estate-related controls.
Act as a constructive and pragmatic business partner while maintaining independent compliance judgment and effective challenge.

Financial planning compliance oversight

Lead the development and ongoing maintenance of the compliance framework supporting the firm’s financial planning offering.
Establish compliance standards for the approved service scope, permitted activities, planner titles and credentials, jurisdictional requirements, client disclosures, fees, conflicts, referrals, privacy and record keeping.
Design risk-based monitoring and testing of financial planning activity, including plan-file reviews, supervision evidence, implementation consistency and remediation.

Assess whether planning information is appropriately reconciled to dealer KYC and whether resulting investment recommendations and actions are consistent with KYP, costs, available alternatives and suitability obligations.
Provide compliance oversight of planning tools, methodologies, assumptions, templates, marketing materials and client communications.
Analyze findings and complaints, identify trends or systemic issues, challenge first-line supervision and escalate material matters to the CCO.
Advise on the compliance implications of new planning services, technology, specialist referrals and changes to the delivery model.

Decision rights and escalation expectations

May establish monitoring and testing methodologies, documentation standards, quality controls and escalation protocols consistent with the approved compliance framework.
May assign and prioritize Compliance resources, review and approve routine work product, and require management responses and remediation evidence.
May close routine findings where satisfactory evidence has been obtained and closure is within delegated authority.
Must escalate material non-compliance, actual or potential client harm, systemic or repeat deficiencies, overdue high-risk remediation, potential reportable events, significant conduct concerns and matters requiring CCO or legal judgment.
Does not replace Branch Management’s first-line supervision, make decisions reserved to the CCO, or commit the firm to a regulatory position unless expressly authorized.

Approved monitoring and testing methodologies, work programs and quality standards
Monitoring, branch review and Operations-control review reports

The CMSO leads five direct reports: four Senior Directors, responsible for Corporate Planning and Governance, Project Management, Growth and Innovation, and Marketing and Communications, and a Project Coordinator/Executive Assistant. Working in a multifaceted environment, the CMSO makes sense of complex and emerging issues, frames them for decisions by the Chief Executive Officer, the Executive Leadership Team, Boards and Committees, and leads the plans, programs and projects that turn strategy into measurable results for members.

THE IDEAL CANDIDATE

The ideal candidate is a senior strategic leader who thrives in complexity, is a strong and effective communicator and has a deep background in corporate governance. The CMSO will turn ambiguous and competing information into clear strategy and plain language so that Boards, elected officials and executives can act on and set priorities across the organization aligning resources where they create the most value. They bring strong business and corporate service acumen along with a delivery focused mindset that can balance delegating vs perfection, and the judgement and diplomacy to advise on sensitive matters. They will also have the experience and background to effectively work with internal and external partners and stakeholders as well as elected officials and various levels of government.

As a true partner and a leader of people, the successful candidate brings strong emotional intelligence, integrity, a corporate services mindset, earns trust, and builds alignment through influence. They adjudicate objectively between competing views, support productive debate, contribute to dialogue constructively, lean into difficult conversations and step in directly when the team is stretched. They coach senior leaders, draw on the experience of the team, model the organization’s values, and strengthen a collaborative, accountable and high-performing culture, staying calm and fact based in a fast-moving, political environment. They also need to be passionate about the work of municipalities and the people they lead.

THE ORGANIZATION

Founded in 1905, Alberta Municipalities (ABmunis) is the province’s largest municipal association. It represents 264 of Alberta’s 334 municipalities, from small summer villages to major cities and specialized municipalities, which together are home to more than 85% of Albertans. It advocates on shared municipal issues and helps members build resilient communities. It also pools its members’ purchasing power to secure better pricing on employee benefits, insurance, energy and other services, with the proceeds helping fund its advocacy work. Its business services and its advocacy reinforce each other, and it works through partnerships to build common solutions with its members.

Governance

Alberta Municipalities is led by a Board of Directors elected by member municipalities during each annual convention. The Board is comprised of representatives from Alberta’s cities, towns, villages, summer villages, and specialized municipalities.

Job Description

Who You Are

The Associate Director, Compliance is the operational leader of SIFI’s Compliance function and is accountable for the day-to-day management, execution and continuous enhancement of the compliance program for its CIRO-regulated mutual fund dealer activities. The role translates the compliance risk assessment and annual plan into effective monitoring, testing, reporting, remediation and regulatory support.

Reporting to the Chief Compliance Officer (CCO), the Associate Director provides technical leadership, provides day to day management of Compliance resources, establishes program standards and quality controls, and escalates material, complex or unresolved matters. The role maintains independent second-line challenge while partnering constructively with the Branch Manager, Operations and other business functions.

Steadyhand Investment Funds Inc. (SIFI) is seeking an Associate Director, Compliance to help lead and continuously enhance its compliance program.

Reporting to the Chief Compliance Officer, this role serves as the operational leader of the Compliance function and manages the day-to-day compliance program for a CIRO-regulated mutual fund dealer. The Associate Director provides leadership across monitoring and testing, branch reviews, registrations, complaints, governance reporting, regulatory examinations, policy management and regulatory change implementation.

The successful candidate will combine technical compliance expertise with people leadership, program management and practical business partnership. This role offers meaningful responsibility and a potential development path toward future Chief Compliance Officer responsibilities.

ROLE BOUNDARY -
This is a second-line compliance leadership role. Day-to-day supervision of Approved Persons, new-account approvals, trade reviews and suitability decisions remain with the Branch Manager role. The Associate Director assesses whether supervisory systems are operating effectively and does not replace first-line supervision.

Responsibilities: What You Will Do/ What You Will Own

Compliance program leadership

Lead the day-to-day operation of the firm’s compliance program and manage execution of the annual compliance plan.
Maintain the compliance risk assessment, compliance calendar and risk-based testing framework.
Establish monitoring methodologies, documentation standards, quality controls and escalation protocols.
Prioritize resources and continually enhance the effectiveness, efficiency and scalability of the compliance function.

Monitoring and testing oversight

Design and oversee risk-based monitoring and testing of compliance and supervisory controls.
Design and oversee risk-based reviews of Operations processes and related controls for compliance, including money and securities movement, books-and-records activities, client reporting and reconciliations.
Review testing results, trends, recurring deficiencies and emerging risks.
Challenge supervisory effectiveness and oversee remediation plans and validation testing.
Escalate material findings, high-risk matters and unresolved issues to the CCO.

Branch review program management

Approve the annual review schedule, risk-based scope and testing approach.
Review and approve branch review reports and assess the significance of findings.
Monitor management responses, remediation commitments and overdue actions.
Ensure branch review coverage remains appropriate as the business evolves.

Registration, licensing and continuing education oversight

Oversee registration, licensing, NRD administration, onboarding and termination activities.
Review complex registration matters, restrictions and outside activity disclosures.
Oversee the continuing education, proficiency, annual training and attestation programs.
Ensure registration and proficiency records remain complete, accurate and regulator-ready.

Complaints, investigations and regulatory reporting

Oversee complaint handling, investigations, resolution recommendations and regulatory event assessments.
Review required regulatory notifications, filings and reporting submissions.
Ensure matters are handled consistently, fairly and within applicable requirements.
Escalate material complaints, reportable events and significant conduct concerns to the CCO.

Regulatory examinations and reviews

Lead operational preparation for CIRO examinations, regulatory reviews, audits and information requests.
Coordinate document production, response drafting, examination logistics and internal stakeholders.
Oversee deficiency responses, remediation plans and progress reporting.
Support the CCO in regulator interactions and on material examination matters.

Regulatory change, policies and training

Monitor regulatory developments and conduct impact assessments and gap analyses.
Coordinate implementation of regulatory changes across policies, procedures, controls and business practices.
Maintain compliance policies, guidance and communications and oversee the annual policy review cycle.
Develop and deliver practical training and awareness initiatives.

Governance and reporting

Prepare clear, decision-useful compliance reporting for senior management and governance forums.
Develop dashboards, metrics and key risk indicators and maintain issue and remediation tracking.
Assist the CCO with annual compliance reporting and other governance materials.
Ensure significant matters are escalated on a timely basis.

Team leadership and development

Manage and develop Compliance Officer(s) and future compliance resources.
Establish clear goals, priorities, performance expectations and quality standards.
Review work product and provide coaching, feedback and mentorship.
Build team capability, accountability and succession depth.

Strategic advisory and broader regulatory support

Advise business leaders on regulatory requirements, compliance risks and practical controls for new initiatives and operational changes.
Provide oversight and guidance across AML, privacy, FATCA/CRS, CASL, marketing and communications, conflicts of interest, personal trading, outside activities, registered plans and estate-related controls.
Act as a constructive and pragmatic business partner while maintaining independent compliance judgment and effective challenge.

Financial planning compliance oversight

Lead the development and ongoing maintenance of the compliance framework supporting the firm’s financial planning offering.
Establish compliance standards for the approved service scope, permitted activities, planner titles and credentials, jurisdictional requirements, client disclosures, fees, conflicts, referrals, privacy and record keeping.
Design risk-based monitoring and testing of financial planning activity, including plan-file reviews, supervision evidence, implementation consistency and remediation.
Oversee controls for planner proficiency, training, continuing education and authorization and assess provincial title-protection requirements as the service expands across jurisdictions.
Assess whether planning information is appropriately reconciled to dealer KYC and whether resulting investment recommendations and actions are consistent with KYP, costs, available alternatives and suitability obligations.
Provide compliance oversight of planning tools, methodologies, assumptions, templates, marketing materials and client communications.
Analyze findings and complaints, identify trends or systemic issues, challenge first-line supervision and escalate material matters to the CCO.
Advise on the compliance implications of new planning services, technology, specialist referrals and changes to the delivery model.

Decision rights and escalation expectations

May establish monitoring and testing methodologies, documentation standards, quality controls and escalation protocols consistent with the approved compliance framework.
May assign and prioritize Compliance resources, review and approve routine work product, and require management responses and remediation evidence.
May close routine findings where satisfactory evidence has been obtained and closure is within delegated authority.
Must escalate material non-compliance, actual or potential client harm, systemic or repeat deficiencies, overdue high-risk remediation, potential reportable events, significant conduct concerns and matters requiring CCO or legal judgment.
Does not replace Branch Management’s first-line supervision, make decisions reserved to the CCO, or commit the firm to a regulatory position unless expressly authorized.

Expected work products and records

Compliance risk assessment, annual plan and compliance calendar
Approved monitoring and testing methodologies, work programs and quality standards
Monitoring, branch review and Operations-control review reports
Issue assessments, remediation plans, validation results and closure records
Registration, proficiency, complaint and regulatory reporting oversight records
Regulatory examination responses, deficiency plans and progress reporting
Compliance dashboards, key risk indicators and governance materials
Regulatory change assessments, implementation plans, policies and training materials
Financial planning compliance framework, testing results and management reporting

Qualifications: What You Must Bring:

Education and experience

University degree in business, finance, law, commerce, economics or a related discipline.
5 – 10 or more years of progressive experience in securities compliance, wealth management, mutual funds, banking or another regulated financial services environment.
Direct experience supporting a CIRO-regulated dealer is strongly preferred.
Experience managing regulatory examinations, compliance reviews, remediation programs and complex regulatory matters.
Prior experience leading, supervising or mentoring compliance professionals.
Experience developing or overseeing compliance for financial planning activities or a financial planning service model is considered a strong asset.

Industry knowledge and credentials

Strong knowledge of CIRO Mutual Fund Dealer requirements and applicable Canadian securities legislation.
Deep understanding of KYC, suitability, registration, supervision, complaints and regulatory reporting requirements.
Knowledge of financial planning designations, provincial title-protection frameworks and the interaction between financial planning, KYC, suitability, conflicts, fees, referrals and recordkeeping is considered a strong asset.
Canadian Securities Course (CSC) and Conduct and Practices Handbook (CPH) are preferred.
Branch Managers Course and additional compliance, risk, audit or governance credentials are assets.

Capabilities

Excellent regulatory judgment, analytical thinking and problem-solving ability.
Clear, persuasive written and verbal communication, including executive-level reporting.
Ability to influence stakeholders, manage competing priorities and make risk-informed decisions.
Strong project management, organizational and change leadership capabilities.

Experience testing or validating automated controls or models
